name: ref_erfc
prose: Precondition: none; x is any double. Postcondition: with hx the high word of x and ix = |hx|: if ix >= 0x7ff00000 it returns (double)((hx >> 31) << 1) + 1/x, i.e. NaN for a NaN, 0 for +infinity and 2 for -infinity. If |x| < 0.84375: for |x| < 2^-56 it returns 1 - x; otherwise it computes y = r/s and returns 1 - (x + x*y) when hx < 0x3fd00000 (every negative x and x < 1/4) and half - (x*y + (x - half)) otherwise. If 0.84375 <= |x| < 1.25 it returns (1 - erx) - P/Q for x >= 0 and 1 + (erx + P/Q) for x < 0. If 1.25 <= |x| < 28: for x <= -6 (ix >= 0x40180000 with the sign set, including x = -6 exactly) it returns two - tiny (reached only when |x| >= 1/0.35); otherwise it forms r from the exp products and returns r/x for x > 0 and two - r/x for x < 0 (so x between -6 exclusive and -1.25). If |x| >= 28 it returns tiny*tiny for x > 0 and two - tiny otherwise. No memory is modified.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_erfc (oracle.c:246-301). Reviewer round 15 is right: for x = -6 the code returns two - tiny (lines 289-290), so the old 'x >= -6' range was wrong. Also added the NaN/inf case at lines 252-255.

name: ref_writelabel
prose: Precondition: the globals lab, bootarea, specname, bbsize, labeloffset, labelsoffset, lba_offset, disable_write, installboot and is_file are set up; if installboot is set, ref_readboot must be able to open and read the boot file (it exits the process through err or errx on open, read or size failure). Postcondition: if disable_write is non-zero it warns, displays the label with ref_display(stdout, NULL) (which uses lab) and returns 0 without changing lab or writing the disk. Otherwise it sets lab.d_magic and d_magic2 to DISKMAGIC, sets d_checksum to 0 and then to dkcksum(lab), calls ref_readboot if installboot is set, adds lba_offset to p_offset of every partition among the first d_npartitions whose p_size is non-zero (modifying lab in place; partitions with zero size are untouched), encodes lab into bootarea at labeloffset + labelsoffset * lab.d_secsize, and opens specname O_RDWR. If the open fails: for is_file it warns and returns 1; otherwise it saves errno, calls ref_geom_class_available("PART") (which can exit via errc(1) if the GEOM tree cannot be read) and returns 1 after warning (with a hint to use gpart(8) if the PART class exists). If the open succeeds it writes bbsize bytes of bootarea; a short or failed write warns, closes the descriptor and returns 1; otherwise it closes the descriptor and returns 0. The descriptor is closed on every path where it was opened.
note: checked oracle.c:370-424. Reviewer round 15 is right: line 388-389 adds lba_offset only to partitions with non-zero p_size, not to every non-zero p_offset. Note d_checksum is computed before the offsets are adjusted.

name: ref_readlabel
prose: Precondition: specname, is_file, bootarea, labeloffset, labelsoffset and the label globals are set up; flag says whether a missing label is fatal. Postcondition: opens specname O_RDONLY (err(1) on failure). If is_file it calls ref_get_file_parms (fstat failure err(4); not a regular file or link errx(4); sets secsize = DEV_BSIZE and mediasize = file size); otherwise it sets mediasize and secsize from g_mediasize and g_sectorsize and calls err(4) if either is negative. It calls errx(1) if mediasize exceeds 0xffffffff * secsize. It seeks to 0 and reads BBSIZE bytes into bootarea (err(4) if the read returns -1, errx(4) if fewer than BBSIZE bytes) and closes the descriptor. It decodes the label from bootarea + labeloffset + labelsoffset * secsize into lab with bsd_disklabel_le_dec, storing the status in error; if flag is non-zero and error is non-zero it calls errx(1). If is_file it returns 0 (even when decoding failed and flag was zero). Otherwise it sets lba to the minimum p_offset over the first d_npartitions partitions whose p_size is non-zero (starting from ~0); if lba != 0 and the RAW_PART offset equals lba, it subtracts lba from p_offset of every partition with non-zero p_size and stores lba in lba_offset; it then returns error (0 for a valid label, non-zero otherwise). The descriptor is closed on all paths that return.
note: checked oracle.c:445-504. Reviewer round 15 is right: the subtraction at 493-496 is guarded by p_size, not applied to every non-zero offset.

name: ref_zone
prose: Precondition: this is the full ref_zone(device, argc, argv, combinedopt, task_attr, retry_count, timeout, verbosemode); device is a valid CAM device and argv/combinedopt are usable by getopt. Postcondition: allocates a CCB (error 1 with a warning if that fails) and parses the options: -a, -c (command name looked up in zone_cmd_map, case-insensitive; ambiguous or unknown gives error 1), -l (strtoull of the whole argument, else error 1), -N, -o (report option lookup) and -P (print flags lookup); other options are ignored. Without -c it returns 1. It calls get_device_type and calls errx(1) if that fails. For the report-zones action it allocates a 64 KiB buffer (err(1) if that fails) and builds a SCSI ZBC IN command or an ATA ZAC/NCQ receive command by device type (build_ata_cmd failure returns its non-zero value after a warning; an unknown device type gives 1); for other actions it builds a ZBC OUT or ATA command similarly. It then sets CAM_DEV_QFRZDIS (and CAM_PASS_ERR_RECOVER when retry_count > 0), sends the CCB (failure: warning and result -1) and checks the CCB status (not CAM_REQ_CMP: error print and result 1). For non-report actions it then returns 0. For report zones it computes the valid length, calls ref_zone_rz_print, and if that returns ZONE_PRINT_MORE_DATA it clears the CCB and cdb_storage and repeats the request from the buffer reset, otherwise a ZONE_PRINT_ERROR result gives 1. On every path that reaches the common exit it frees the CCB (if allocated), the data buffer and cdb_storage and returns the result: 0, 1, -1 or the non-zero value from build_ata_cmd.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_zone (oracle.c:319-671); the slice is only the second half. Checked every goto bailout and the restart_report loop.

name: ref_Transform
prose: Precondition: buf points to four UINT4 words and in points to sixteen UINT4 words, not overlapping; both are readable and buf is writable. Postcondition: static void. It copies buf[0..3] into a, b, c, d, runs the 64 MD5 steps (four rounds of 16 FF, GG, HH or II steps, each reading one word of in and adding a constant), then adds a, b, c, d to buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3] respectively using UINT4 arithmetic. in is only read, not written. There is no return value and no other side effect.
note: slice cut the head: the function is ref_Transform (oracle.c:199-295), not MD5Transform. Checked lines 199-295.

name: ref_nametokva
prose: Precondition: name is a string; iocfunc is a callable ioctl function pointer; opts is the global option word. Postcondition: strncpy copies at most sizeof(res.ipfu_name) bytes of name into the request (the destination is not NUL-terminated if name is at least that long) and the result address starts as NULL. If OPT_DONTOPEN is not set in opts it opens IPL_NAME O_RDONLY and returns NULL if that fails. It then calls (*iocfunc)(fd, SIOCFUNCL, &res), ignoring the return value, with fd = -1 when OPT_DONTOPEN is set, closes fd if it is non-negative, and returns res.ipfu_addr, replacing a NULL address with (ipfunc_t)-1. Any descriptor it opened has been closed before it returns.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_nametokva (oracle.c:249-270). Returns at 262 (NULL) and 269.

name: ref_main
prose: Precondition: argc and argv come from the C runtime; getprogname() decides the personality (a name containing 'halt' sets dohalt, 'nextboot' sets donextboot). Postcondition: it calls ref_usage (which exits 1) for an unknown option or leftover arguments; errx(1) when the no-shutdown file exists (unless -f or nextboot), for conflicting options, and for -r with other options; for -D it exits 0 if the nextboot file does not exist, otherwise unlinks it (warning on failure) and exits 0. A non-nextboot caller with a non-root euid gets err(1) with EPERM. With -q it calls reboot(howto) and, if that returns, err(1). With -k and no -f it checks that /boot/<kernel>/kernel exists and is a regular file (err or errx(1) otherwise). If any environment was collected it calls ref_write_nextboot; the nextboot personality then exits 0. Otherwise it logs the action (unless -l), records a shutdown utmpx entry, syncs (unless -n), ignores several signals and: for -r it sends SIGEMT to init, calling err(1) if kill fails and otherwise returning 0 from the function (the only return statement, line 448); in the normal case it sends SIGTSTP to init (err(1) on failure), SIGTERM to all processes (err(1) unless ESRCH), waits and syncs, sends SIGKILL repeatedly (jumping to restart on a kill error other than ESRCH, warning if processes remain after 5 rounds), and calls reboot(howto). If reboot(2) returns, or a kill error sent control to restart, it sends SIGHUP to init and calls errx(1) with the saved errno text (prefixed '(can't restart init): ' if the SIGHUP also failed). So the function never returns except the reroot case returning 0, and otherwise ends in an exit call.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_main (oracle.c:240-502). Old prose said it never returns and lists exit 0 after a successful reboot(2); the reroot branch returns 0 at line 448 and reboot(2) does not return on success.

name: ref_main
prose: Precondition: argc and argv as passed to main. Postcondition: if argc < 2 it returns ref_veriexec_usage() (prints usage, returns 0). It opens _PATH_DEV_VERIEXEC write-only into dev_fd and parses options with getopt: -h returns ref_veriexec_usage() (0); -C stores the directory; -i queries the state (err(EX_UNAVAILABLE) if the device is not open or the ioctl fails; errx(EX_USAGE) for an unknown state name) and exits with (x & state) == 0; -l (when HAVE_VERIEXEC_GET_PATH_LABEL is defined) prints labels and exits EX_OK; -S enables strict validity checking; -v increments Verbose; -x checks paths and exits 0 or 2; -z modifies the state: 'debug' (a prefix match) needs a following level 'off' or an integer 0..INT_MAX (errx(EX_USAGE) otherwise), other names are mapped by ref_veriexec_state_modify; it then needs an open device (err(EX_UNAVAILABLE)), issues the ioctl (err(EX_UNAVAILABLE) on failure), prints the debug level or the state in octal, and exits EX_OK; any other option calls ref_veriexec_usage and exit(EX_USAGE). After the options it prints the verbosity if set, exits with err(EX_UNAVAILABLE) if the device is not open, opens the log, errx(EX_OSFILE) if ve_trust_init() < 1, optionally reads the veriexec version, loads each remaining manifest argument with ref_veriexec_load (err(EX_DATAERR) if one fails) and finally calls exit(EX_OK). It returns only in the two usage cases (value 0); all other paths end in exit, err or errx.
note: slice cut the head: real function is ref_main (oracle.c:178-310). Old prose gave only 'EX_OK or nonzero'; the usage returns of 0 (lines 185 and 194) are now stated.

name: ATOMIC_OPS(add)
prose: Generated function arch_atomic_add(int i, atomic_t *v), produced by ATOMIC_OP(add, addl) inside ATOMIC_OPS(add) (atomic.h:38-52, 156-166). Precondition: v points to a valid atomic_t. Postcondition: it runs a load-locked/store-conditional loop: ldl_l temp from v->counter, addl temp, i, temp, stl_c temp back, and branches back to retry if the store-conditional failed; on exit v->counter is its previous value plus i (32-bit add) with no concurrent update to the counter lost. It returns nothing and the asm has no memory clobber or barrier (it is a relaxed operation). The same ATOMIC_OPS(add) invocation also generates arch_atomic_add_return_relaxed, arch_atomic_fetch_add_relaxed and the arch_atomic64_ add variants, which are separate functions.
note: checked atomic.h:37-52 and 156-165. Reviewer round 15 only notes that the invocation also generates other functions; they are separate items, so the prose for arch_atomic_add itself stays.

name: ffs
prose: Precondition: none; word is any int. Postcondition: static inline function with attribute const. Returns 0 when word is 0; otherwise it returns __ffs(word) + 1, i.e. 1 plus the index of the least significant set bit of word, a value from 1 to 32 (the int is sign-extended to unsigned long, which does not change the lowest set bit). The function has no side effects.
note: checked bitops.h:376-380. The old formal contract was rejected by random testing (false for word = 65536); contract left empty because the result depends on __ffs (cmpbge/ctz) architecture intrinsics.

name: io7_init_hose
prose: Precondition: io7 points to a valid struct io7 and port is a valid port index of it; runs at init time (__init). Postcondition: returns nothing. It allocates a pci_controller with alloc_pci_controller (memblock_alloc_or_panic, no NULL check), sets hose->index to the next value of a static counter and, for index 0, sets pci_isa_hose; stores the io7_port csrs and hose pointers and hose->sysdata; allocates io_space and mem_space resources with alloc_resource and fills in the bases, config space base and the IO and MEM resource ranges, names and flags; requests ioport_resource for the IO range and iomem_resource for the MEM range, printing a KERN_ERR message and continuing if either request fails; saves the four POx_WBASE, POx_WMASK and POx_TBASE values into io7_port->saved_wbase, saved_wmask and saved_tbase; calls marvel_pci_tbi(hose, 0, -1); creates the ISA scatter-gather arena (8 MB at 8 MB) into hose->sg_isa and the PCI arena (up to 1 GB at 3 GB) into hose->sg_pci with iommu_arena_new_node, dereferencing both without a NULL check and setting align_entry = 8; programs window 0 as scatter-gather, window 1 as direct-mapped (__direct_map_base, __direct_map_size, TBASE 0) and window 2 as scatter-gather, disables window 3 (WBASE[3] = 0), clears bit 61 of POx_CTRL, prints 'FIXME: disabling master aborts' and clears bits 14-15 of POx_MSK_HEI, and calls marvel_pci_tbi(hose, 0, -1) again. The hose and resources are owned by the kernel and never freed here.
note: slice cut the head and the name was wrong: the function is io7_init_hose (core_marvel.c:202-330); marvel_init_hose does not exist. The old precondition (hose given as an argument) was wrong: the function allocates the hose itself.

name: titan_agp_info
prose: Precondition: none beyond kernel init state; no parameters. Postcondition: searches for an AGP port: pachip0's a_port gives hosenum 2 if titan_query_agp reports AGP present; otherwise, if pchip1 is present and its a_port reports AGP, hosenum is 3. It then looks for the hose with that index in the hose list and returns NULL (allocating nothing) if there is none (this includes hosenum -1, no AGP port) or the hose has no sg_pci arena. It then kmallocs an alpha_agp_info (GFP_KERNEL) and returns NULL if that fails. Otherwise it fills hose, private = the AGP port, ops = &titan_agp_ops, aperture bus_base 0, size 0 and sysdata NULL, capability lw 0 with rate 3, sba 1 and rq 7, and mode lw 0 with rate = 1 << apctl_v_agp_rate, sba = apctl_v_agp_sba_en, rq 7 and enable = apctl_v_agp_en read from the port's pctl.csr, and returns it; the caller owns the allocation.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE3(pciconfig_iobase, long, which, unsigned long, bus, unsigned long, dfn)
prose: Generated function __do_sys_pciconfig_iobase(which, bus, dfn). Precondition: when IOBASE_FROM_HOSE is clear and bus and dfn are both 0, pci_isa_hose must be non-NULL; for a found device dev->sysdata must be non-NULL; for IOBASE_ROOT_BUS the chosen hose's bus pointer must be non-NULL. Postcondition: if (which & IOBASE_FROM_HOSE) the hose is the first in hose_head whose index equals bus, else -ENODEV if none; otherwise, if bus == 0 and dfn == 0 the hose is pci_isa_hose, else dev = pci_get_domain_bus_and_slot(0, bus, dfn) (-ENODEV if NULL), the hose is dev->sysdata and the device reference is released with pci_dev_put before the switch. Then by (which & ~IOBASE_FROM_HOSE) it returns hose->index (IOBASE_HOSE), sparse_mem_base, dense_mem_base, sparse_io_base, dense_io_base, or hose->bus->number (IOBASE_ROOT_BUS), and -EOPNOTSUPP for any other selector. No reference is held on return.
note: checked pci.c:412-452. Reviewer round 15 is right: IOBASE_ROOT_BUS dereferences hose->bus (line 449), so the precondition now says it must be non-NULL.

name: common_shutdown_1
prose: Precondition: generic_ptr points to a struct halt_info (mode and restart_cmd, which may be NULL); the function is the on_each_cpu callback and runs on every CPU. It makes no assumption about whether interrupts are enabled on entry. Postcondition: it calls local_irq_disable() and never re-enables interrupts. It locates this CPU's per-cpu HWRPB flags and clears 0x00ff0001. With CONFIG_SMP on a CPU other than boot_cpuid it sets the 'remain halted' flag (0x40000), stores the flags, clears this CPU from the present and possible masks and calls halt() (no return). On the boot CPU, if mode == LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART it sets the cold bootstrap flag (0x20000) when restart_cmd is NULL and the warm bootstrap flag (0x30000) otherwise; for any other mode it sets 'remain halted'; it stores the flags. With CONFIG_SMP it clears the boot CPU from the present and possible masks and spins until the present mask is empty. If alpha_using_srm: with CONFIG_DUMMY_CONSOLE it calls irq_exit() if in a hard IRQ, takes the console lock, takes over the console with dummy_con and unlocks; then it calls pci_restore_srm_config() and set_hae(srm_hae). It then calls alpha_mv.kill_arch(mode) if set. If !alpha_using_srm and mode != LINUX_REBOOT_CMD_RESTART it returns (with local interrupts still disabled). Otherwise it calls srm_paging_stop() when alpha_using_srm and then halt().
note: checked process.c:75-163. Reviewer round 15 is right: on_each_cpu runs callbacks with interrupts disabled, so the old 'interrupts enabled' precondition was wrong. Older reviewers (non-SRM non-restart path returns; no loop) are right and the prose says it returns.
